To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
high and low achiever students have different self-perceptions and that these perceptions change over time.

the high achievers had significantly higher self-ratings than the low achievers in three of five general areas of student self-perception: (1) learning in class; (2) study habits and attitudes and (3) peer relationships.

high achievers rate themselves higher on self-perceptions than low achievers, that both groups show improvement on self-perceptions over a semester, that high achievers show more improvement than low achievers on some self-perceptions and the same improvement as low achievers on others, and that the interaction between group and time is statistically significant for some self-perceptions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the differences in self-perceptions between high and low achieving students.
the self-ratings of high and low achieving students on a variety of characteristics which are thought to be important for quality learning.

a study of the self-perceptions of high and low college students, with particular emphasis on the differences and similarities between the two groups and the effects of a semester of college on their self-perceptions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
high achievers tend to rate themselves higher on all characteristics of quality students than do low achievers.

the quality student is a high achiever who is well-organized, has good study habits, has a good relationship with his peers, is a good student-instructor relation, and has good physical and emotional health.
high achievers are self-assured, confident, and self-reliant, and low achievers are insecure, uncertain, and dependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

high achievers tend to be more self-critical and less satisfied with their own performance than low achievers. (Author/AM)
